history.period: Within the Salasar Balaji Temple, founded 1754 (the Ram Darbar upper sanctum's own date is not established in sources - verify)
history.summary: IDENTITY/AMBIGUITY FLAG: 'Shri Ram Darbar, Salasar' is NOT an independent temple - it is the Ram Darbar shrine on the UPPER part of the sanctum of the famous Salasar Balaji Temple (seq 2110, id salasar-balaji), with the bearded-and-moustached Hanuman (Balaji) idol below it at the feet of Shri Ram. Recommend merging into the Salasar Balaji entry (2110) or documenting it as a sub-shrine, not a standalone temple row. The Balaji temple itself was founded by the devotee Mohandas Ji Maharaj in 1754 (Shravan Shukla Navami, Samvat 1811) after a Jat farmer of Asota village (Nagaur) unearthed the swayambhu Hanuman idol while ploughing; the present Rajasthani-style structure is built of brick, lime, cement, mortar, stone and marble, with gold-and-silver mosaic work in the sanctum, sabha mandap and circulatory path. Two big annual fairs (Chaitra and Ashwin Purnima) draw lakhs of devotees.

name: Shri Ram Darbar, Salasar
town_description: Salasar is a small town in Churu district, Rajasthan, near Sujangarh on the Jaipur-Bikaner highway. It grew around the famous Salasar Balaji Temple (Hanuman) and is a major pilgrimage halt in the Shekhawati region of Rajasthan.

travel.railway: Sujangarh railway station is nearby; Jaipur is the nearest major railhead (verify).
travel.road: On the Jaipur-Bikaner highway, in the heart of Salasar town near Sujangarh (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Chaitra Purnima (Mar-Apr) and Ashwin Purnima (Sep-Oct) fairs are the grandest.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published in the sources consulted (verify locally); the Balaji temple generally opens early morning to evening.
